permission.description: Hand an http, https or mailto link to the operating system's default handler. The command refuses every other scheme, so this cannot name a local program to launch. It opens a link and returns nothing: it reads no file, runs no chosen executable and tells the caller nothing about the machine.

Open this application's own address in the default browser. The launcher supplies the address; a caller may only add a path within the app, and anything that is not a clean local path is dropped in favour of the home page, so this cannot send anybody off the local origin.

Show a file from this workspace in the operating system's file manager. The caller names a path, and the command opens the FOLDER that holds it rather than the file, so nothing here launches a program by extension. The path is canonicalised and must resolve inside the data folder this launcher's own backend stores files in, so a page cannot name a system folder or a network share. It reports nothing back about the machine beyond whether the folder was opened.
Open the launcher's own diagnostic log in the default handler. The path is resolved by the launcher and cannot be supplied by the caller.
Read the local address the application is being served on, which is the address of the page asking for it.
Turn the update check on or off, which is the choice offered by the update notice.
Record that the user does not want to be told about one particular version again.

Read which application server this window is talking to and which of the four configuration layers decided it. Reads no file the caller names and reports nothing about the machine beyond the address of the page asking, which the page already knows.

Save which application server the launcher should use from the next start, or clear that choice. The address is validated by the launcher before it is stored, and the setting is only ever read while starting, so this cannot repoint a running window. This is the one permission here that changes what the application does on the next run rather than what it does now, and it is deliberately NOT granted to a server whose address a user typed in: see capabilities/app-window.json.

Record a choice of a server on this computer and restart into it. This is the way out of a configured server that cannot be reached, so it is granted to the launcher's own startup failure screen. It takes no argument and can only ever move the launcher towards the default it shipped with.

set.description: Everything the launcher's own documents may call: the splash screen, the startup failure screen and the update notice. These documents are served by the launcher itself over the Tauri protocol, so this set is granted to the local origin only. It is the full command list on purpose, because that is exactly what the local origin could already reach before the application declared any permissions at all, and this file must not quietly take something away while it is adding the declaration.
